name: Colorado
one: Colorado mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Colorado, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Monday, October 26Passed

To get your ballot by mail, register or update your record (including your mailing address) no later than 8 days before the election: Monday, October 26, 2026. After that, you can still register and vote in person at a voter service and polling center through Election Day, but no ballot will be mailed to you. (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be in the hands of your county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Postmarks do not count. If you are not sure it will arrive by mail in time, drop it off. (official page)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Colorado’s own site

At school away from home, in Colorado or in another state? What Colorado says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No request and no reason are needed: every registered voter in Colorado is mailed a ballot automatically, at the mailing address on their voter record. You can vote in person instead if you prefer. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. There is nothing to request. To make sure your ballot goes to the right place (for example a school or temporary address), check or change the mailing address on your voter record at GoVoteColorado.gov. Open it (official page)
  • In person. If your ballot did not come, or you lost or damaged it, ask your county clerk for a replacement, or vote in person at a voter service and polling center. (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it early enough to reach the county clerk by 7 p.m. on Election Day; a postmark is not enough. (official page)
  • Drop box. Drop boxes are open 24 hours a day and watched by video; teams of election judges from both parties collect the ballots. Your county clerk lists the places. (official page)
  • In person. Hand it in at one of your county's drop-off locations by 7 p.m. on Election Day; your county clerk lists them. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the envelope; the Secretary of State's pages ask only for your signature and do not mention a witness. If you registered for the first time, you may need to send a copy of your ID with the ballot; your county's instructions in the ballot packet will say so. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Colorado’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Monday, October 19, 2026 to Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Voter service and polling centers must be open from at least 15 days before the election (Monday, October 19, 2026) through Election Day, except Sundays and the first Saturday of that stretch. You can register and vote there in person. (official page)

Students

At school in Colorado, away from home

The Secretary of State says it is up to the student to decide where they live for voting: your residence is your main home, the place you mean to return to whenever you are away, and you may have only one. A student living elsewhere in Colorado can stay registered at home and change the mailing address on their record so the ballot is mailed to school, or register at the school address if that is now home. (official page)

At school in another state, with Colorado as home

The Secretary of State says this is the student's decision: a Colorado resident at college out of state may keep their registration in their hometown and vote by mail. A student who registers in another state is no longer eligible to vote in Colorado. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters away from Colorado (and their spouses, civil union partners and dependents) and Coloradans living abroad can ask to get their ballot by mail, fax or email, or download it online. Their ballot must be sent by 7 p.m. Mountain Time on Election Day. A mailed ballot counts if it reaches the county by the close of business on the 8th day after Election Day; because that day, November 11, is Veterans Day, the state's 2026 calendar lists the last day as Thursday, November 12, 2026. An emailed or faxed ballot must arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)

Colorado in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The 2026 Election Calendar states its dates as rules (for example "through the 8th day before an election"); the dates here were worked out from those rules for November 3, 2026. The calendar calls itself a reference guide only.
  • If the county finds a problem with your signature or a missing ID, the 2026 Election Calendar gives you until 11:59 p.m. Mountain Time on Wednesday, November 11, 2026 (8 days after Election Day) to fix it; the county must write to you about it.
  • Drop box and voter service and polling center places and hours are set by each county clerk.
  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program's state guide was read through the content feed its own page loads.
